newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan crash probe officials to visit Indonesia.
newsitem.headline: Japan crash probe officials to visit Indonesia.

text.p: Japan's Transport Ministry will send a team of investigators to Indonesia next week as part of an investigation into the crash of a Garuda Indonesia plane in southwestern Japan in June, officials said on Friday.
The team, which will visit Indonesia from October 13 to 20, aims to re-question the crew of the Garuda DC-10 and investigate the airline's flight operations system, the ministry said.

The investigators will follow up on an earlier ministry inquiry which indicated that a fire in an engine under the right wing triggered the accident, which killed three people and injured 99 at Fukuoka airport on June 13.
The pilot to aborted takeoff after reaching takeoff speed, causing the plane with 260 passengers and a crew of 15 to overshoot the runway and slide to a fiery halt in a field.
Garuda stopped using the McDonnell Douglas Corp DC-10s on its Japanese routes after the crash in response to a request by the Japanese government, Indonesia's Antara news agency reported in July.
